<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918734_theRebbe_176" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918734_theRebbe_176__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar for the second day of Shavuos 5728.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">The second day of the festival of Shavuos, 5728.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the Alter Rebbe's question on the verse "And G-d spoke all these words, saying: I am..." and his answer that the Ten Commandments contain the entire Torah in a general principle, which is then detailed.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And G-d spoke all these words, saying: I am..."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Alter Rebbe</t>
    <t s="2">questions the meaning of "all these words,"</t>
    <t s="3">for seemingly it should have said, "And G-d spoke, I am..."</t>
    <t s="4">And he explains,</t>
    <t s="5">that "all these words" refers</t>
    <t s="6">to the entire Torah,</t>
    <t s="7">including everything that a veteran student will innovate in the future.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is "And G-d spoke all these words,"</t>
    <t s="9">for in the Ten Commandments</t>
    <t s="10">("I am...")</t>
    <t s="11">the entire Torah is included</t>
    <t s="12">("all these words").</t>
    <t s="13">And this can be connected with Rashi's commentary on the verse,</t>
    <t s="14">that what is written "all these words"</t>
    <t s="15">(before "I am...")</t>
    <t s="16">teaches that all the Ten Commandments were said</t>
    <t s="17">(initially)</t>
    <t s="18">in one utterance,</t>
    <t s="19">and afterwards each and every commandment was explained individually.</t>
    <t s="20">For the content of both explanations is,</t>
    <t s="21">that the giving of the Torah was in a manner of general principle and detail.</t>
    <t s="22">However, according to Rashi's explanation, the verse speaks of the Ten Commandments themselves,</t>
    <t s="23">that initially they were said in a general aspect</t>
    <t s="24">(one utterance)</t>
    <t s="25">and afterwards each and every commandment was detailed individually.</t>
    <t s="26">And according to the Alter Rebbe's explanation, the verse speaks of the details of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="27">that they too were given initially in a general aspect,</t>
    <t s="28">in the Ten Commandments,</t>
    <t s="29">and afterwards they were detailed and drawn down into revelation.</t>
    <t s="30">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="31">that even this itself</t>
    <t s="32">(the detailing and revelation of the Ten Commandments)</t>
    <t s="33">was in a manner of general principle and detail.</t>
    <t s="34">For the beginning of the drawing down and detailing of the Ten Commandments is in the Written Torah,</t>
    <t s="35">and afterwards it is detailed more specifically in the Oral Torah,</t>
    <t s="36">for the entire Oral Torah is the explanation</t>
    <t s="37">and elucidation of the Written Torah</t>
    <t s="38">("From where are these matters? The verse says..."),</t>
    <t s="39">and the Oral Torah itself is also in a manner of general principle and detail,</t>
    <t s="40">Mishnah, Beraisa,</t>
    <t s="41">Gemara, etc., until everything that a veteran student will innovate.</t>
    <t s="42">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="43">since all the details of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="44">up to everything that a veteran student will innovate,</t>
    <t s="45">were all given to Moshe at Sinai,</t>
    <t s="46">why were they not given from the outset in a revealed manner,</t>
    <t s="47">and why were they given initially in a general aspect.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the creation of the world also followed a pattern of general principle and detail, as the general utterance of "Bereishis" contained all subsequent utterances.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood</t>
    <t s="2">from what we find similarly regarding the creation of the world</t>
    <t s="3">("He looked into the Torah and created the world"),</t>
    <t s="4">that it was in a manner of general principle and detail.</t>
    <t s="5">For our Sages said,</t>
    <t s="6">"With ten utterances the world was created... could it not have been created with one utterance?"</t>
    <t s="7">And it is known</t>
    <t s="8">that the "one utterance" is the utterance of "Bereishis"</t>
    <t s="9">("Bereishis is also an utterance"),</t>
    <t s="10">which is a general utterance that includes the nine utterances that follow it.</t>
    <t s="11">For this is what is written,</t>
    <t s="12">"In the beginning G-d created the heavens and the earth," and our Sages said,</t>
    <t s="13">"'the heavens' to include their hosts, and 'the earth' to include its hosts,"</t>
    <t s="14">that all creations came into being from the utterance of "Bereishis"</t>
    <t s="15">(as it is a general utterance that includes all the utterances).</t>
    <t s="16">However, they were in a general aspect,</t>
    <t s="17">and afterwards the utterance of "Bereishis" was detailed in the nine utterances that follow it,</t>
    <t s="18">and through this the creations came into being in a manner of division into details.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
